Hi Eleni — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then details below.

Summary (short):
- Measurement window: rolling 7-day window for production availability SLOs; 30-day rolling for monthly targets on billing-oriented SLAs.
- Planned maintenance: excluded from uptime if communicated >= 48 hours in advance and scheduled during the agreed maintenance policy window; exclusions are logged via our change-control process and reflected in the monthly SLA report.
- Monitoring & customer access: we expose a read-only Grafana SLO dashboard (link below) and provide a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint for customers under Dedicated/Private contracts; hosted customers get the read-only dashboards + API SLO reports. Alerts are routed to PagerDuty integrations you configure.

Detailed notes:
1) Measurement definitions
   - Availability: measured as successful 2xx/3xx responses to the inference endpoint across all regions weighted by requests. We compute 1 - (failed_tokens/total_tokens) over a rolling 7-day window for live SLO enforcement (this is our primary operational SLO). For contractual reporting we provide rolling 30-day and calendar-month aggregates.

   - Latency: P90/P95 measured on request wall-clock time from ingestion to final token emitted. For burst/queued requests we report queuing separately. If you need a hard tail SLA (e.g., P99), we can add that as an addendum.

2) Planned maintenance and exceptions
   - Exclusion policy: maintenance windows are excluded if (a) a customer-visible maintenance page is posted, (b) we provide >= 48 hours notice, and (c) the window is scheduled in our change-management system and shared with customer contacts. We log an "exclusion token" for each event and it appears in the monthly SLA calculation output.

   - Emergency maintenance: for emergency maintenance (P0 mitigation), time is not excluded automatically; we review on a per-event basis and provide adjustment only after post-incident review with artifacts.

3) Monitoring & access
   - Dashboards: read-only Grafana for SLOs and latency percentiles (https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/DeltaSystems/SLO-overview).
   - Metrics: internal metrics are emitted via Prometheus; hosted customers receive a periodic SLO report and can request a scheduled export. Dedicated / Private deployments can have a dedicated metrics endpoint or a Grafana service account with viewer permissions.
   - Alerts: we support PagerDuty, Opsgenie, and email routing. Alert rules and thresholds are configurable per-route as part of onboarding.

4) Evidence artifacts and attachments
   - I've attached our SLO matrix that maps metric names to dashboard panels and measurement windows (redwood_slo_matrix_v1.xlsx).

Next steps: Laura (cc'd) will coordinate any contractual language with your legal team. Marcus is copied to confirm the technical details on the change-control tokens and to provide a sample monthly SLA report export.

If you want, we can schedule a short 30-minute call to walk through the dashboard and the SLO math.

Thanks Priyom — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from ops/legal:

- Our security policy requires that any maintenance window excluded from SLA must be formally logged and agreed in writing 72 hours prior to the window start. Your 48h threshold may be acceptable but legal asked whether you can make it 72h for enterprise customers in the contract.
- We need a sample of the monthly SLA export CSV (or a small sample file) showing how exclusions and incidents are applied to the calculation. Can Marcus send an example?
- For the read-only Grafana view: can users be assigned by email address or does access require service accounts? Ideally we want SRE and compliance to have separate viewer groups.

If you can provide the sample export + confirm the 72h option for enterprise contracts, we can move the SLA redline forward.

Regards,
Eleni

Hi Eleni — Marcus here (SRE). Quick answers inline: 

- Advance notice: We can accommodate a 72-hour contractual requirement for Enterprise customers; our internal policy remains 48h for platform ops but contractually we'll put 72h for planned maintenance carve-outs. We'll include change-control proof (RFC id, scheduled window, and notification list) in the monthly export.

- Sample export: attached is a redacted sample CSV that shows how incidents and exclusions map to the rolling window calculation. Columns: timestamp_start,timestamp_end,total_requests,failed_requests,exclusion_flag,exclusion_reason,calculated_availability.

- Grafana access: for Dedicated and Private customers we support both service-account-based viewer tokens and invite-by-email for read-only roles. For hosted accounts we'll provide role-based viewer groups keyed by email. We can map SRE and Compliance to separate teams and provide scoping to dashboards/panels.

Attached: sla_sample_export_redacted.csv (CSV stub attached to the thread).

If you want a walkthrough I can share my screen and step through the export and the exclusion markers.
